beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps the image dense while a shared compact thought process updates it across recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image carrier from the compact process that reads and updates it. The encoder first turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing groups those features without dropping the spatial field. DQ-CTM then applies shared ticks to update the carrier. The decoder turns the updated dense field into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier with shared DQ-CTM ticks
params.note: The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines a dense feature field first, then partitions that field into windows while keeping every token.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as a dense feature field produced from the low-resolution image. The encoder maps the input image into that field. The window partition then turns the same field into tokens without discarding them.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before it is windowed

terms.label: encoder applied to the low-resolution image
window partition of the dense feature field

beats.intent: Among the five reported methods, DQ-CTM-SR has the second largest parameter count rather than being the smallest model.
beats.narration: The parameter counts should be read as a size comparison, not as a blanket compactness claim. CATANet is the smallest reported model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is only slightly larger at 0.550 million. IMDN comes next at 0.715 million. DQ-CTM-SR is 1.129 million parameters, the second largest of the five. CARN is largest at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest reported model
params.note: Bars are ordered from smallest to largest.
